title: Lab weekly research capture — quant + eval + onboarding
content:
Week: 2027-09-20 / Sprint week boundary
Owners: Maya Chen (notes), Ibrahim Noor (bench lead), Celia Park (eval lead)

Summary (one line): focused week on narrowing PTQ failure modes for 7B/13B variants, running end-to-end evals for onboarding rw-7b-ptq-lite, and finishing latency profiling for prefix-KV cache interactions. Some promising latency gains with dynamic KV eviction; still seeing hallucination regressions on few-shot summarization.

Attendees (standup + deep-dive):
- Maya Chen (applied-ml)
- Ibrahim Noor (inference infra)
- Celia Park (evals)
- Rafael Gomez (model-onboarding)
- Priya Nair (SLOs / cost analysis)
- Guests: Ben Liu (serving-runtime) joined for KV discussion

Decisions made this week:
- Ship rw-7b-ptq-lite to canary on dedicated pools for internal integration tests (canary window 48h). Rationale: cost/latency profile meets threshold; still behind on quality for public rollout. (Action: Rafael to open deployment PR)
- Use hybrid PTQ+QAT patch for sensitive attention layers on 13B (experimental): freeze first 6 layers, apply 4-bit PTQ elsewhere. (Action: Ibrahim + Maya to prototype)

Experiments run (high level):
1) Model: rw-7b-ptq-lite (PTQ 8-bit, per-channel scale, L2 calibration)
   - Dataset: mix of summarization + code completion test sets (2.4k prompts)
   - Metric highlights: Rouge-L micro average dropped 2.8 pts vs float32 on few-shot summarization; perplexity delta +0.9.
   - Latency: host-serving median token latency 26ms (vs float 36ms) on a g4dn-equivalent benchmark harness.
   - Memory: peak GPU memory 5.4GB (vs float 11.8GB).
   - Observations: beam-chosen answers sometimes truncate complex lists; prefix-KV reuse helps, but cache eviction at 512-token boundary introduces discontinuities.

2) Model: rw-13b-open-ptq (aggressive symmetric 6-bit, group size 64)
   - Dataset: open-domain QA + instruction following (1.6k prompts)
   - Metric highlights: pass@1 for code tasks down 6% (regression concentrated on long-context refactoring prompts).
   - Latency: 48ms median token. Cost/unit estimate ~0.42x original.
   - Notes: Quant noise concentrated in late-layer attention matrices; exploring per-head clipping.

3) KV eviction microbench (runtime env): dynamic eviction policy vs fixed-size cache
   - Throughput: +12% effective tokens/sec for mixed short-long workload when using dynamic eviction tuned on sequence-length histogram.
   - Tail latency: 95th percentile reduced by 18% under bursty traffic.
   - Actionable: integrate simple histogram-based eviction as opt-in in runtime (Ibrahim to prototype), add perf flag to canary.

Evals (Celia):
- Eval harness completed: 6 named suites (summ, code, chat-consistency, toxicity, instruction-following, math) with automated diffing.
- New failure mode tracker created (sheet + alert): tracks prompt/seed combos where quality regresses >5% relative to baseline.
- Top 3 regression clusters this week: list-truncation on summarization, hallucination on instruction-following (factual recall), numeric instability on math tasks.

Model onboarding status (Rafael):
- rw-7b-ptq-lite: onboarding checklist 80% complete. Integration tests pass but UX sanity tests pending (token streaming edge cases).
- rw-13b-open-ptq: blocked on quality gating (see above); will try hybrid QAT patch next.
- Data access and SLO: confirm where we store calibration maps and quant metadata (KMS tagging required for private deploys). Rafael to file infra ticket.

Risks / Blockers:
- Quality regressions are not uniform; some prompts catastrophic (hallucinate) while most pass. Need targeted unit tests to catch these early.
- Calibration data pipelines slow (batch calibration took 7h on the small cluster) — slows iteration.
- KV cache eviction edge-case causing token duplication in streaming mode; affects few customers in internal integration tests.

Open questions / research threads:
- Is per-head quant clipping more robust than layer-wise clipping for late-attention regressions? (Celia + Maya to run probe)
- What is the minimal PTQ calibration set size that yields <2pt Rouge-L drop? (experiment: downsample calibration to 2%, 5%, 10%)
- Can we create a synthetic prompt suite that reliably triggers truncation failures for regression monitoring?

Action items (owner + ETA):
- Rafael: open canary PR for rw-7b-ptq-lite (infra + deployment flags) — ETA: 2027-09-22
- Ibrahim: prototype histogram-based KV eviction opt-in in runtime (bench harness + perf regression) — ETA: 2027-09-27
- Celia: add unit tests to eval harness for list-truncation and hallucination clusters; create alert rule in NewRelic/Datadog — ETA: 2027-09-24
- Maya + Ibrahim: prototype hybrid PTQ+QAT for 13B sensitive layers (small local experiment) — ETA: 2027-09-30
- Priya: cost delta slide for leadership (include per-token cost, mem savings, expected annualized savings for hosted tier) — ETA: 2027-09-28

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal):
- Might try small QAT on just layernorm + attention-out projections; keep all input embeddings float32 for stability.
- Consider staging datasets by prompt type (e.g., list-heavy, math-heavy) to pinpoint regressions faster.
- Add a small 'canary-quality' run in CI that runs 100 curated prompts through any new quant build before it canary-deploy. Could be gated by ML-3421.

Links / refs: see linked_artifacts above. Also: shared folder with raw bench logs (S3): s3://redwood-internal-applied-ml/bench/2027-09-20/

Retro notes (what went well):
- Faster turnaround on infra experiments (Ibrahim reduced harness bootstrap time by ~30%).
- Eval harness catching clusters early — saves manual triage.

Retro notes (what to improve):
- Better calibration pipeline; avoid 7h slow path. Automate sampling + warm-start calibrations.
- More consistent naming across quant artifacts (use artifact-tag schema: model-version.quant{bits}.calib{hash})

Next meeting focus: hybrid PTQ/QAT feasibility results, KV eviction prototype results, and failed-prompt miniset generation.

-- Maya
